intro_html: In New Orleans, red beans and rice is a Monday dish. Monday was wash day, the pot could sit on the back of the stove all morning while you worked, and it used up the ham bone from Sunday. That is a budget tradition older than any of us, and it still holds up. Beans, the holy trinity of onion, celery, and bell pepper, smoked sausage, and rice. Cheap, filling, and better on day three than on day one, which is exactly what you want out of a meal prep.
cost_closing_html: About $3.32 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a Louisiana classic that gets better every day it sits in your fridge.
shop_smart: Canned kidney beans are the shortcut worth taking. Dried beans are cheaper per ounce, but they need a soak and an hour of babysitting. If you have the time, the dried bag saves real money on a batch this size.
Smoked sausage is the flavor engine, so buy the rope. Pre-sliced costs more per pound for a cut you can make in thirty seconds.
Onion, celery, and bell pepper are the trinity and they are not optional. Bell peppers are the priciest of the three, so buy them when the multi-packs are on sale and freeze the extras chopped.
Your spice rack is doing most of the seasoning here. Thyme, oregano, paprika, bay leaves, and a Cajun blend are jars you already own, and they cost a fraction of what a boxed red beans mix does.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the smoked sausage into coins and brown them in the vegetable oil in a large pot, then set them aside.
Add the diced onion, celery, and green bell pepper to the same pot and cook until softened and the bottom of the pot picks up color.
Stir in the garlic and the dried seasonings and cook for a minute so the spices bloom in the fat.
Add the kidney beans with their liquid and the chicken broth, then return the sausage to the pot.
Simmer uncovered for at least forty minutes, mashing some of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the gravy.
Cook the rice separately according to the package while the beans simmer.
Fish out the bay leaves, season with salt and black pepper to taste, and serve the beans over the rice.
portion_html: Weigh the rice and the beans separately. Put each pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1, and divide by 14 so every container gets the same rice base and the same ladle of beans. Every serving lands near 581 calories with 25 grams of protein. The beans thicken overnight, so add a splash of water when you reheat.

head.description: Louisiana red beans and rice with smoked sausage, rebuilt for 14-serving meal prep with the holy trinity and Cajun spices. 581 calories, 25g protein, about $3.32 per serving (at everyday cost).

steps: Slice and brown the smoked sausage, then set it aside.
Cook the onion, celery, and bell pepper in the same pot until soft.
Add garlic and dried seasonings and bloom them in the fat.
Add the beans, broth, and sausage and simmer at least forty minutes, mashing some beans to thicken.
Season, remove the bay leaves, and portion beans over rice into 14 containers.
